metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And all the AI neural networks are graphs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Do some computations send the result here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: do another computation, do a data transformation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: do a merging, do a pooling, do another computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Is it possible to compress and say

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: how we make this thing efficient,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: this whole process efficient, this different?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So first, the fundamental elements in the graphs

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: are things like matrix multiplies, convolutions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: data manipulations, and data movements.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So GPUs emulate those things with their little singles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: basically running a single threaded program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And then there's an NVDA calls it a warp

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: where they group a bunch of programs

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: that are similar together for efficiency

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and instruction use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And then at a higher level, you take this graph

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and you say this part of the graph is a matrix multiplier

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: which runs on these 32 threads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: But the model at the bottom was built for

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: running programs on pixels, not executing graphs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So it's emulation, ultimately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So is it possible to build something

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: that natively runs graphs?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Yes, so that's what TenStore did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Where are we on that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: How, like in the history of that effort,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: are we in the early days?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Yeah, I think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: TenStore, it's started by a friend of mine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Lebesha Bajik, and I was his first investor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So I've been kind of following him

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and talking to him about it for years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And in the fall when I was considering things to do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: I decided, you know, we held a conference last year

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: with a friend who organized it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And we wanted to bring in thinkers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And two of the people were Andrei Karpathy

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and Chris Latner.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And Andrei gave this talk, it's on YouTube,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: called Software 2.0, which I think is great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Which is, we went from programs computers

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: where you write programs to data program computers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: You know, like the future of software

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: is data programs, the networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And I think that's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And then Chris has been working,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: he worked on LLVM, the low level virtual machine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: which became the intermediate representation

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: for all compilers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And now he's working on another project called MLIR,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: which is mid-level intermediate representation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: which is essentially under the graph

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: about how do you represent that kind of computation

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and then coordinate large numbers

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: of potentially heterogeneous computers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And I would say technically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Tense Torrent's two pillars are those two ideas,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Software 2.0 and mid-level representation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: But it's in service of executing graph programs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: The hardware is designed to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So it's including the hardware piece.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And then the other cool thing is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: for a relatively small amount of money,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: they did a test chip and two production chips.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So it's like a super effective team.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And unlike some AI startups,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: where if you don't build the hardware

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: to run the software that they really wanna do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: then you have to fix it by writing lots more software.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So the hardware naturally does matrix multiply,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: convolution, the data manipulations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and the data movement between processing elements

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: that you can see in the graph,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: which I think is all pretty clever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And that's what I'm working on now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So I think it's called the Gray's Call of Processor

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: introduced last year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: There's a bunch of measures of performance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: We're talking about horses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: It seems to outperform 368 trillion operations per second.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Seems to outperform Nvidia's Tesla T4 system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So these are just numbers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: What do they actually mean in real world performance?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: What are the metrics for you that you're chasing

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: in your horse racing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: What do you care about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Well, first, the native language of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: who write AI network programs is PyTorch now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: PyTorch, TensorFlow, there's a couple others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Do you think PyTorch has won over TensorFlow?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Or is it just-

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: I'm not an expert on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: I know many people have switched

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: from TensorFlow to PyTorch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And there's technical reasons for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And I use both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Both are still awesome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Both are still awesome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: But the deepest love is for PyTorch currently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Yeah, there's more love for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And that may change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So the first thing is when they write their programs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: can the hardware execute it pretty much as it was written?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So PyTorch turns into a graph.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: We have a graph compiler that makes that graph.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Then it fractions the graph down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So if you have big matrix multiply,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: we turn it into right size chunks

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: to run on the processing elements.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: It hooks all the graph up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: It lays out all the data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: There's a couple of mid-level representations of it

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: that are also simulatable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So that if you're writing the code,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: you can see how it's gonna go through the machine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: which is pretty cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And then at the bottom, it schedules kernels,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: like math, data manipulation, data movement kernels,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: which do this stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So we don't have to write a little program

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: to do matrix multiply,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: because we have a big matrix multiplier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Like there's no SIMD program for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: But there is scheduling for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So one of the goals is if you write

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: a piece of PyTorch code that looks pretty reasonable,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: you should be able to compile it, run it on the hardware

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: without having to tweak it

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and do all kinds of crazy things to get performance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: There's not a lot of intermediate steps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: It's running directly as written.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Like on a GPU, if you write a large matrix multiply,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: naively, you'll get five to 10%

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: of the peak performance of the GPU.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And then there's a bunch of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: who publish papers on this, and I read them about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: what steps do you have to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And it goes from pretty reasonable,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: well, transpose one of the matrices,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: so you do row ordered, not column ordered,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: you know, block it so that you can put a block

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: of the matrix on different SMs, you know, groups of threads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: But some of it gets into little, little details.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Like you have to schedule it just so,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: so you don't have register conflicts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So they call them kuda ninjas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Kuda ninjas, I love it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: To get to the optimal point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: you either write a pre, use a pre-written library,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: which is a good strategy for some things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: or you have to be an expert

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: in micro architecture to program it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Right, so the optimization step

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: is way more complicated with the GPU.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So our goal is if you write PyTorch,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: that's good PyTorch, you can do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Now there's, as the networks are evolving,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: you know, they've changed from convolutional

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: to matrix multiply,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: where people are talking about conditional graphs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: they're talking about very large matrices,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: they're talking about sparsity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: they're talking about problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: that scale across many, many chips.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So the native, you know, data item is a packet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Like, so you send a packet to a processor,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: it gets processed, it does a bunch of work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Silvio Macaulay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: Let's start with the big and the basic question. What is a blockchain and why is it interesting?

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: Why is it fascinating? Why is it powerful? All right. So a blockchain, think of it, is

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: really a common database distributed. Think about it as a ledger in which everybody can write an

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: entry in a page. You can write, I can write, and everybody can read. And you have a guarantee

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: that everybody has the same copy of the ledger that is in front of you. So whatever you see on

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: page seven, anyone else sees on page seven. So what is extraordinary about this is this common

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: knowledge thing that I think is really a first for humanity. I mean, if you look at communication,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: like right now, you can communicate very quickly images, thoughts, or photos. But do you have a

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: certainty that whatever you have received has been received by everybody else? Not really.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And so this common knowledge and the certainty that everybody can write, nobody has been

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: prevented from writing whatever they want. Nobody can erase, nobody can tear a page of a ledger,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: nobody can swap page, nobody can change anything. And that is immutable common record is extremely

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: powerful. And there's something fundamental that is decentralized about it. So at least in spirit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: to some degree, or against maybe a resistance to centralization. Absolutely. If it is not

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: decentralized, how can it be common knowledge? If only one person or a few people have a ledger,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: the only way you don't have a ledger, you have to ask, what is on page seven? And how do you know

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: that whatever they tell you is on page seven, they tell the same thing to everybody else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And so this common knowledge is extremely powerful. Just to give you an example, assume that

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: you do an auction. You have worked very hard, you build a building, and now you want to auction off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: It makes sense because you want to auction worldwide, better yet you want to tokenize

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: the building and sell it in parcels. Now everybody sees the bids and you know that everybody sees the

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: bids. You and I see the same bids and so does everybody else. So you know that a fair price

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: has reached and you know who owns what and who has spent how much. And if you do it instead of

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: a wise, you know, in a centralized system, I put a bid saying, oh, congratulations, Alex, you won.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And your price is $12,570. I don't know. So if instead of this common knowledge is a very powerful

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: tool for humanity. So we return to it from a bunch of different perspectives, including like a

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: technical perspective, but you often talk about blockchain and some of these concepts of

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: decentralization, scalability, security, all those kinds of things. But one of the most maybe

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: impactful, exciting things that leverage the blockchain, this kind of ledger idea of common

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: knowledge is cryptocurrency. So in the financial space. So is there, can you say in the same kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: of basic way, what is cryptocurrency in the context of this common knowledge and in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: context of the blockchain? Great. Cryptocurrency is a currency that is on such a ledger. So imagine

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: that on the ledger, initially, you know that somehow say you and I are the only owner of each one. Let's

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: give it to ourselves a billion each of whatever this unit. Then I start writing on the ledger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: I give a hundred of these units to my sister. I give this much to my aunt. And then now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: because it's written on the ledger and everybody can see, my sister can give 57 of these units

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: that she received from me to somebody else. And that is money. And that is money because

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: you can see that somebody who tenders your payment has really the money there. You don't have any

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: more of a doubt when you want to sell an item. If I write you a check, is the check covered?

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: Or do I have the money at the moment of a transaction? You really see because the ledger

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: is always updated. What you see is what I see, the merchant sees. You know that the money. So

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: the most powerful money system there is because it is totally transparent. And so you know that

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: you have been paid and you know that the money is there. You have not to second guess anything else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: So the common knowledge applied there is you're basically mimicking the same kind of thing you

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: would get in the physical space, which is if you give a hundred of that thing, whatever,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: of that cryptocurrency to your sister, the actual transfer is as real as you giving like a basket

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: of apples to your sister. Because so in the case in the physical space, the common knowledge is in

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: the physics of the atoms. And then it's digital space, the common knowledge is in this ledger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And so that transfer holds the same kind of power, but now it's operating in the digital space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: Go ahead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: Again, I apologize for a set of ridiculous questions, but you mentioned cryptocurrencies

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: and money. What is money? Why do we have money? Do you think about this kind of from this high

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: philosophical level at times of this tool, this idea that we humans have all kind of came up with

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: and seem to be using effectively to do stuff? Money is a social construct, okay, in my opinion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And this has been somehow people always felt that somehow money is a way to allow us to transact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: even though we want to different things. So I have two sheep and then you have one cow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And I want the cow, but you are looking for blankets instead. So to have money is really

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: simplifies this. But at the end of it, that's why a bit was invented. And you start with gold,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: then you start to win the congee, then you start to win the check. But at the end of the day,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: money is essentially a social construct because you know that what you receive, you can actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: spend with somebody else. And so there is a kind of a social pact and social belief that you have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: At the end of the day, even a barter requires these beliefs that other people are going to accept

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: the quote unquote currency you offer them. Because if I'm a Mason and you ask me to build a wall

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: in your field, and I did, and you in exchange, you give me a thousand sheep,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: what am I going to do? Eat them all? No, I have to feed them. And if I don't feed them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: they die and my value is zero. So in receiving these livestock, I must believe that somebody else

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: will accept them in return for something else. So my is this social belief, social shared belief

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: system that makes people transact. That's fascinating. I didn't even think about that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: that you're actually, you have a deep network of beliefs about how society operates. So the

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: value is assigned even to sheep based on that everyone will continue operating how they were

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: previously operating. Somebody will feed the sheep. I didn't even think about that. That's

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: fascinating. So that directly transfers to the space of money and then to the space of digital

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: money and cryptocurrency. Okay. Does it bother you sort of intellectually when this money that is a

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: social construct is not directly tied to physical goods, like gold, for example?

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: Not at all, because after all, gold has some industrial value. Nobody delights it. It's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: metal, it doesn't oxidate. It has some good things about it. But does this industrial value really

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: represent the value to which it now is traded? No. So gold is another way to express our belief.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: I give you an answer. Gold, you treat it like, oh, somebody else will want this for doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: something else. So it is really this notion of this money is a mental construct and is shared,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: it's a social construct, I believe. And so some people feel that it's physical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: so therefore gold exists. But then as you know now, countries, most sophisticated country right now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: they print their own money and you believe that they are not going to exaggerate it with inflation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: Not everybody believes it. But I'm saying there is at least, they are not going to exaggerate it

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: blatantly. And therefore you receive it because you know that somebody else will accept it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: will have a faith in the currency and so on and so forth. But whether it's gold, whether it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: livestock, whatever it is, money is really a shared belief. So there is something, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: and I've been reading more and more about different cryptocurrencies. There is a kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: belief that the scarcity of a particular resource like Bitcoin has a limited amount

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: and it's tied to physical, you know, to proof of work. So it's tied to physical reality in terms

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: of how much you can mine effectively and so on, that that's an important feature of money. Do you

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: think that's an important feature to be a part of whatever the money is? That is certainly a very

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: useful part. So at some point in time, you know, assume that money is something that all of a sudden

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: we say daisies are money, are the currency. Then, you know, I offer you 10 daisies in payment of

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: whatever goods and services you want to provide. But at the end of the day, if you know that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: can cultivate it and generate them at will, then perhaps, you know, you should not accept my payment

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: in here is a bouquet of daisies. So you need some kind of scarcity, the inability to create

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: suddenly out of nothing is unimportant. And it's not an intrinsic necessity, but it's much easier

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: to accept once you know that there is a fixed number of units of whatever currency there is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And therefore you can mentally understand I'm getting, you know, this much of a piece of a pie

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: and therefore I consider myself paid. I understand what I'm receiving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: You describe the goals of a blockchain, you have a nice presentation on this, as scalability,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: security and decentralization. And you challenge the blockchain trilemma that claims you can only

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: have two of the three. So let's talk about each. What is scalability in the context of blockchain

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: and cryptocurrency? What does scalability mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: So remember, we said that the blockchain is a ledger and each page receives a, gets transaction

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: and everybody can write in this, in these pages of a ledger. Nobody can be stopped for writing

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: and everybody can read them. Okay. Scalability means how fast can you write? Just imagine that

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: you can write an entry in this special shared ledger once every hour. Well, you know, what are

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: you going to do if you have an O1 transaction per hour, the world doesn't go around. So you need to

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: add to have scalability means here that you can somehow write a lot of transaction and then you

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: can read them and everybody can validate them. And that is the speed and the number of transactions

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: on per second and the fact that they are shared. So you want to have this, this, the speed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: not only in writing, but in sharing and inspection for validity. This is scalability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: The world is big. The world wants to interact with the people, want to interact with each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And you better be prepared to have a ledger in which you can write lots and lots and lots of

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: transactions in this special way. Very, very, very quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: So maybe from a more mathematical perspective, or can we say something about how much scalability

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: is needed for a world that is big? Well, it really depends how many transactions

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: you want. But remember that I think right now you have to go into at least a thousand

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: transactions per second. Even if you look at credit cards, we are going to go from an average

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: So it's very important to do that. And that is the quintessential problem in a blockchain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And people have thought about it to say it's not me, it's not you. But for instance, in proof of

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: Oh, beautifully said. Thanks for sharing. This is great. Yes. I totally understand you.

body.input: It's a struggle. You've accomplished some incredible things in the space of science,

body.input: in the space of technology, in the space of theory and engineering. Do you have advice

body.input: for somebody young, an undergraduate student, somebody in high school, or anyone who just feels

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: young about life or about career, about making their way in this world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: So I was telling before that I believe in emotion and my thing is to be true to your own emotion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And I think that if you do that, you're doing well because it's a life well spent and you are

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: going never tired because you want to solve all these emotional knots that have always intrigued

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: you from the beginning. And I really believe that to live meaningfully, creatively, and to

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: live your emotional life. So I really believe that whether you're a scientist or an artist even more,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: but a scientist, I think of them as artists as well. If you are a human being, so you are really

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: to live fully your emotions and to the extent possible, sometimes emotions can be overbearing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And my advice is try to express them with more and more confidence. Sometimes it's hard, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: you are going to be much more fulfilled than by suppressing them. What about love? One of the big

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: ones, what role does that play? That's the bigger part of emotions. It's a scary thing, right? It's

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: a lot of vulnerability that comes with love, but there is also so much energy and power and

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: love in all senses and in the traditional sense, but also in the sense of a broader sense for

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: humanity, this feeling of compassion that makes us one with other people and the suffering of other

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: people. I mean, all of this is very scary stuff, but it's really the fabric of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: Well, the sad thing is it really hurts to lose it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: Yes. That's why the vulnerable comes with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: That's the thing about emotion is it's the up and down and the down seems to come always with the

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: unfortunately, we humans are mortal or appear to be for the most part. Do you think about your

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: thing because that is the best motivation to live fully. What do you hope your legacy is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: You mentioned you have two kids. Yes. And so I really feel that there is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: on one side is my biological legacy and that is my two kids, right? And their kids hopefully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And that is one thing. And the other thing is this common enterprise, which is society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: And I really feel that my legacy would be better by providing security and privacy. Actually,

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: for me, are metaphorical to say, I want to give you the ability to interact more and take more

body.input: not only in a transaction, like it would be a blockchain transaction, but that is really

body.input: tackle. And ultimately privacy and security is freedom. Freedom is at the core of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: It's dangerous. It's like the emotion thing. But ultimately that's how we create all the

metadata.title: Podcast: Silvio Micali: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain, Algorand, Bitcoin & Ethereum | Lex Fridman Podcast #168

body.input: that death provides and us anxious beings create cool stuff along the way. Is there a deeper meaning

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: And now here's my conversation with my dad, Alexander Friedman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: What to you is the most beautiful idea in physics, chemistry, or mathematics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Oh, let's go to that place first before we go to the to Kiev.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: The most beautiful in physics, chemistry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: I would say Einstein, his ideas regarding stochastic motion and Browning motion, I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: it is the most beautiful, clear, simple idea because from this stochastics, you can prove

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: existence of molecules, believe me or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: It was, I think it was his first publication in 1905 with his first wife.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Actually, it was significantly her idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: That's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: They were collaborators.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Those five, four, five papers he published.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Yeah, actually almost everything which Einstein did, it was published, the most important

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: stuff, they were published in one year, 1905.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: But the first idea was probably the most elegant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Can you describe Brownian motion and why you think it's beautiful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: You see that people at that time, they understand that if molecules, if they exist, their motion

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: is absolutely chaotic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Boom, boom, boom, boom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: What he proved that doesn't matter what size of particles is, their motion is similar and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: about the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: So it is not necessary to see molecules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: You can look at bigger particles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Like if you smoke, there is particles and you can see like a propagation of this smoke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: And from here, determine behavior of molecules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: And that's actually relatively short, very elegant, very clear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: And at that point, people, they kept talking about molecules, but it was no proof because

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: there is no like a super electronic microscope to see them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: So, you know, I'm saying, yes, molecules exist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: You said, well, I mean, can you show me that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: So Einstein made it and he proved and a lot of people after this publication said, hmm,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: probably molecules really exist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Einstein 1905.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: So what do you like about that idea?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: The simplicity of proving something very, very, very, very, very, very complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: So if I ask you, for example, you know, molecules exist, can you prove it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Obviously, like now you would say, okay, I have a special electronic microscope and I

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: can take a look.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: That's a molecule.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: But when you go back to beginning of 20th century, people, they were laughing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Can you prove something?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: No, you cannot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: No, no, no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Take a look.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: It's something very simple, very, very simple, very, very simple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: What do you think it takes to do that kind of thinking and come to those ideas?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: And how many times have you encountered those kinds of ideas in your life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Have you had any?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Yeah, I would say that's a, that's a whole beauty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: My feeling that's a whole beauty of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: It's just, you know, people, they say, no, no, no, no, it's too, it's impossible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Or and you say, no, no, wait, take a look, take a look.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Wait a second.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Read it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Take a look.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Just think for five minutes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: If something is very complicated, you know, Capitza, Nobel Prize laureate, like I work

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: with him, by the way, he used to say, if it is complicated, it's probably wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Well, it was a lot of discussion between Capitza and Landau because Landau, he, he enjoyed

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: to do something in a most complicated way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: he used to say, well, this is simple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: It means this is right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: And now he was like, okay, you mean that everything was simple is right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: I mean, like Feynman too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: He liked the simple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: And that's the whole point to find this simplicity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]

body.input: That's, that's the beauty of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman Podcast #100 – Alexander Fridman: My Dad, the Plasma Physicist [Reupload]
