metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: You never saw it. How can you not say you know? It's a seminal film in American history to those

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: people who care. It shows you Kubrick had a pacifist, thank God, anti-war mentality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: which he showed in Paz of Glory as well as Strangelove. It's such a dire, well-done

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: scenario that I wanted Mr. Putin to be aware of the way the United States thinks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Yeah, the absurdity of escalation, the absurdity of war at the largest scale,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: the absurdity of nuclear war especially. Can we walk back from the brink of nuclear war?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Can we?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Can we?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Yes. Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: What's the path to walk back?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Between who and who?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Reason and diplomacy. There's no reason. I mean, talk to the guy. Mr. Biden, why don't you calm down

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: and go and talk to Mr. Putin in Moscow? Why don't you just sit across the table from him

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: and try to have a discussion without falling into ideologies and stuff like that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Can I ask you for advice? You did some of the most difficult interviews ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Do you have advice that you can give to someone like me or anyone hoping to understand something

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: about a human being sitting across from them about what it takes to do a good interview?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: You're doing one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Well, no, but there's a, listen, there's levels to this game and interviewing somebody like

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Vladimir Putin, also language barrier, sit across from the man, try to keep it simple,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: try to keep an open mind. Try to also ask challenging questions, but not challenging

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: with an agenda, but seeking to understand and understand deeply. How do you do that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Seeking the truth. It's very simple. Seeking the truth. Being a questioner like you are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: you want to know what is really going on. I could not get anywhere with Biden or Bush

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: or for that matter, Obama. They'd be opaque with me. There's no interview possible with the

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: president of the United States because he's got to stand for all the stuff that they stand for,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: which is imperialism, which is control of the world. How can you defend that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: No one's going to come out and say that. They're always going to blame the enemy. They're going to

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: blame Iran. They're going to blame China. So some people, it may not be possible to break

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: through the opaque. I mean, have you ever seen an interview with the president besides being

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: personable where he actually discussed American policy? Yeah. I mean, not really,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: but maybe after their president, I could see Obama being able to do such an interview. I could see

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: George W being able to do such an interview, or are they not able to reflect at all on the-

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: George W hasn't shown much conscience in terms of thinking about what he's done. You've seen that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: You ever see my movie W? I think that's one of my best movies because it shows a man who's just out

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: of his depth and has no- He has a conscience at the end of the movie, if you remember correctly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: He talks to his wife and he says, I don't get it. I'm trying to do good in the world. I believe in

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: good and right. Why do people not understand that kind of complaint as if he can't get outside

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: himself to understand the way other people think? Empathy, walking like a dramatist is what I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: You walk in the footsteps of other people. When I did a movie about Richard Nixon,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: it wasn't because I liked him. It was because I wanted to- I think I understood a part of him

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: because of my father and I think I wanted to walk in his footsteps. That's not to say I sympathize

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: with him because I didn't. I don't think he helped the American cause at all, but it was empathize as

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: opposed to sympathize. Same thing with Bush. People were shocked when I did the Bush movie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: They said, how can you be in any way receptive to this guy? I said, that's wrong. Dramatists

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: don't have political positions. They walk in the shoes of. That's why Bush movie perhaps was

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: surprising to many people who didn't care for it. Maybe that's what- but you've got to go there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: If you did a movie about a villain, you have to go there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: You have to walk in their shoes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: They usually- Villains usually see themselves as the hero.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: So you have to consider what is it like to live in a world where this person is the hero.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Is that a burden? Is that hard?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Not for George W. Bush. He's bitching because they didn't understand him,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: but he had a good vision, he said, of democracy. Democracy forgives a lot of sins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Can I ask you a hard question on that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Yes, sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: So because empathy is so important to a great interview, let's ask the most challenging

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: version of empathy, which is when you're sitting across from a man on the brink of war that

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: leads to tens of millions of deaths, which is Hitler. So if you could interview Hitler in 1939,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: as the drums of war start to beat, or 1941, when they're already full on war, but there's still a

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: lot of pacifists, there's still a lot of people unsure what are the motivations behind what Hitler

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: is doing, how would you do that interview?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Well, it depends when you do it. If you do it in 1938, I certainly would have... No,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: if you sit down across from Hitler, you empathize. What is your beef? Where have you been? What is

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: your consciousness? Why do you hate Jewish people? All these questions that come up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: his sense of grievance as a result of World War I, there's justifications there, etc.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: And by the way, Churchill was trying to make a deal with him in 1938. That's a fact that people

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: don't know, Churchill himself. There was still the desire in England to make peace with Germany,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: and it was seen as a possible... What Churchill really wanted was Hitler to go against Russia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: and anything to destroy the Bolsheviks. So he was using Hitler as much as he could to go after

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Russia, but Hitler was too elusive to pin him down. But if you remember, Hitler was very kind at the

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: end of the... Kind is not the right word, did not go after the British Empire when he had France,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: and he could have. He had another objective, which was obviously the East. So Hitler's goal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: I think... He always had an admiration for England, it's an interesting story, always.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: And the Empire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Yes. And certainly Churchill, we have no doubts now from history revisionism that

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Churchill's interest, main interest was not Germany, it was the British Empire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: And preserve it to India, the road to India and all that, and Middle East. Churchill fought the

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: entire war with the concept of preserving the British Empire. All his goals, he sent America

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: on a goose chase into Italy, you could argue, instead of establishing a sincere second front

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: in Western Europe. Interesting man. So I would have tried to get... I think I would approach it

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: the same way. In 1939, it would have been a different story because at that point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: he'd attacked Poland and in 1940, France. So it's another ballgame. But certainly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: if at whatever point you talk to him, I would try to understand his point. So I'm not judging you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Hitler. I'm saying to you, tell me what you're thinking. Why are you invading Russia? What's

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: your thought? That's all an interviewer should do. He shouldn't be expressing his contempt for

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Hitler, which like an American journalist interviewing Putin, I'm getting brownie points

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: for expressing my contempt for you. That doesn't wash with me, that's ugly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Yeah, seek to understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Yes. This is a technical question, but was language a barrier as an interviewer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: To some degree. It's very hard to learn Russian. But they have excellent translators in the Kremlin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: excellent. They are people who are trained very seriously for months or years before they... These

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: people are young and they're very bright. I was very impressed with the Russian translator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: It's interesting. I'm impressed as well, but there's a humor that's lost. There's a wit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: a dry wit. There's stuff said between the lines. That's not actually how much content, but it's more

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: the things that make communication more frictionless. There's a sadness to a Russian

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: humor that permeates all things and that sometimes is lost in translation. The translation is a

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: little bit colder, meaning it just conveys the facts. Would you call it sardonic humor?

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: I would say so, yeah. It's interesting. But I think you could see that from facial expressions

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: when you're sitting across from the person and you can feel it. Let me ask you in general,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: what's the role of love in the human condition in your life, in life in general? You looked at some

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: of the darkest aspects of human nature. What's the role of this, one of the more beautiful

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: aspects of human nature? I think without love, I don't think I'd be able to carry on. I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: that love is my... Love is the greatest... The ability to love is the greatest virtue you can

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: have. It's the ability to share with another, with your family, with your children, with your wife,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: with your lover, your partner. It's an ability to extend yourself into the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: and it brings empathy with it. If you love well, I think you expand it to the human race too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: It's the strength behind the great novelists, the great artists of our time. I think part of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: reason I suppose we're scared of science sometimes is because the scientists sometimes don't express

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: that clearly. You can lose that when you focus on the facts, on empirical data, on the science of

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: science. You can lose the humanity that's between the lines. I'm often struck by when I talk to

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: scientists and I've talked to a few, that how arrogant they can be about... They don't talk

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: to you if you don't understand their world and they talk to each other and there's an arrogance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: a closed circle kind of thing. Oh, he's not at my level. There's no discussion to be had with this

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: person. He's a human being. That arrogance is terrifying to me because it's next door neighbor

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: to closed mindedness, which then can be used by charismatic leaders as it was in Nazi Germany

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: to commit some of the worst atrocities. The scientists can be used as pawns in a very cruel

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: game. What advice would you give to young people? You've done, first of all, some of the greatest

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: films ever. You've lived a heck of a life. You were fearless and bold in asking some really

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: difficult questions of this world. What advice would you give to young people today, high school,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: college, about career, how to have a career they can be proud of or how to have a life they can

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: be proud of? Well, I have three children, so obviously I'm not necessarily the best

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: advisor in the world. I do find that the children, I've raised them with a sense of freedom and they

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: do what they want. In the end, it's their life, their destiny, their character. That's what comes

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: out. You can try to influence it, but you can try to get your daughter to wake up at a certain hour

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: in the day, but it never works. I long ago gave up on that and my children are all grown now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: But aside from that, I think if I was a teacher in a school and teaching film, I'd say to the students,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: get an education. You can't just look at film because it's not a full education. It's not the

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: spectrum. I don't think you should teach film as a... I think you need a base in other worlds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: One of the greatest courses I took at NYU was, and I was a war veteran on the GI Bill,

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: so I was older than the other students. I took a class outside the film school in Greek classics

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: because I hadn't had much history and I wanted to know more about the world of Homer and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: The teacher opened my eyes to so much in that class and I wrote about it in my memoir. It's called

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: Chasing the Light about Professor Leahy and what he did to me. He gave me the concepts clearly of

metadata.title: Podcast: Oliver Stone: Vladimir Putin and War in Ukraine | Lex Fridman Podcast #286

body.input: consciousness, which is the Homeric theme of Odysseus and also lethe, L-E-T-H-E, which is sleep,

body.input: The following is a conversation with Rajat Manga.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: He's an engineer and director at Google, leading the TensorFlow team.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: TensorFlow is an open source library at the center of much of the work going on in the world in deep learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: both the cutting edge research and the large scale application of learning based approaches.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: But it's quickly becoming much more than a software library.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: It's now an ecosystem of tools for the deployment of machine learning in the cloud, on the phone, in the browser,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: on both generic and specialized hardware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: TPU, GPU and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Plus, there's a big emphasis on growing a passionate community of developers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Rajat, Jeff Dean and a large team of engineers at Google Brain are working to define the future of machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: with TensorFlow 2.0, which is now in alpha.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: I think the decision to open source TensorFlow is a definitive moment in the tech industry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: It showed that open innovation can be successful and inspire many companies to open source their code to publish

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: and in general engage in the open exchange of ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: This conversation is part of the Artificial Intelligence podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: If you enjoy it, subscribe on YouTube, iTunes or simply connect with me on Twitter at Lex Friedman, spelled F-R-I-D.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Rajat Manga.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: You were involved with Google Brain since its start in 2011 with Jeff Dean.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: It started with this belief, the proprietary machine learning library and turned into TensorFlow 2014, the open source library.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So what were the early days of Google Brain like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: What were the goals, the missions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: How do you even proceed forward once there's so much possibilities before you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: It was interesting back then when I started or when you were even just talking about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: The idea of deep learning was interesting and intriguing in some ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: It hadn't yet taken off, but it held some promise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: It had shown some very promising and early results.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: I think the idea where Andrew and Jeff had started was what if we can take this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: what people are doing in research and scale it to what Google has in terms of the compute power and also put that kind of data together, what does it mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And so far, the results had been if you scale the compute, scale the data, it does better and would that work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And so that was the first year or two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Can we prove that out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And with this belief, when we started the first year, we got some early wins, which is always great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: What were the wins like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: What were the wins where you were, there's some problems to this, this is going to be good?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: I think there are two early wins where one was speech that we collaborated very closely with the speech research team, who was also getting interested in this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And the other one was on images where we, you know, the cat paper, as we call it, that was covered by a lot of folks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And the birth of Google Brain was around neural networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: That was so it was deep learning from the very beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: That was the whole mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So what would in terms of scale, what was the sort of dream of what this could become?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Like what were their echoes of this open source TensorFlow community that might be brought in?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Was there a sense of TPUs?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Was there a sense of like machine learning is not going to be at the core of the entire company is going to grow into that direction?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Yeah, I think so. So that was interesting. And like, if I think back to 2012 or 2011, and first was can we scale it in in the year or so we had started scaling it to hundreds and thousands of machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: In fact, we had some runs even going to 10,000 machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And all of those shows great promise in terms of machine learning at Google.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: The good thing was Google's been doing machine learning for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Deep learning was new. But as we scale this up, we showed that yes, that was possible and it was going to impact lots of things like we started seeing real products wanting to use this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Again, speech was the first. There were image things that photos came out of and then many other products as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So that was exciting. As we went into with that a couple of years externally, also academia started to, you know, there was lots of push on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Okay, deep learning is interesting, we should be doing more and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And so by 2014, we were looking at, okay, this is a big thing. It's going to grow. And not just internally, externally as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Yes, maybe Google's ahead of where everybody is, but there's a lot to do. So a lot of this start to make sense and come together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So the decision to open source, I was just chatting with Chris Glattner about this, the decision to open source with TensorFlow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: I would say for me personally, seems to be one of the big seminal moments in all of software engineering ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: I think that's when a large company like Google decides to take a large project that many lawyers might argue has a lot of IP.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Just decide to go open source with it and then so doing lead the entire world and saying, you know what, open innovation is a pretty powerful thing and it's okay to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: That was, I mean, that's an incredible moment in time. So do you remember those discussions happening?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Whether open source should be happening? What was that like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: I would say I think the initial idea came from Jeff, who was a big proponent of this. I think it came off of two big things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: One was research wise, we were a research group. We were putting all our research out there if we wanted to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: We were building on others research and we wanted to push the state of the art forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And part of that was to share the research. That's how I think deep learning and machine learning has really grown so fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So the next step was, okay, now would software help with that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And it seemed like there were existing a few libraries out there, Tianno being one, Torch being another and a few others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: But they were all done by academia and so the level was significantly different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: The other one was from a software perspective, Google had done lots of software that we used internally and we published papers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Often there was an open source project that came out of that, that somebody else picked up that paper and implemented and they were very successful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Back then, it was like, okay, there's Hadoop, which has come off of tech that we've built.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: We know the tech we've built is way better for a number of different reasons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: We've invested a lot of effort in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And turns out we have Google Cloud and we are now not really providing our tech, but we are saying, okay, we have Bigtable, which is the original thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: We are going to now provide HBase APIs on top of that, which isn't as good, but that's what everybody's used to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So there's like, can we make something that is better and really just provide, helps the community in lots of ways, but also helps push the right, a good standard forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So how does cloud fit into that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: There's a TensorFlow open source library and how does the fact that you can use so many of the resources that Google provides and the cloud fit into that strategy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So TensorFlow itself is open and you can use it anywhere, right? And we want to make sure that continues to be the case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: On Google Cloud, we do make sure that there's lots of integrations with everything else and we want to make sure that it works really, really well there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: You're leading the TensorFlow effort.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Can you tell me the history and the timeline of TensorFlow project in terms of major design decisions, like the open source decision,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: but really what to include and not. There's this incredible ecosystem that I'd like to talk about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: There's all these parts, but what if you just some sample moments that define what TensorFlow eventually became through its,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: I don't know if you were allowed to say history when it's just, but in deep learning, everything moves so fast in just a few years is already history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Yes, yes. So looking back, we were building TensorFlow. I guess we open sourced it in 2015, November 2015.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: We started on it in summer of 2014, I guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And somewhere like three to six late 2014, by then we had decided that, OK, there's a high likelihood we'll open source it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So we started thinking about that and making sure we're heading down that path.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: At that point, by that point, we had seen a few lots of different use cases at Google.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So there were things like, OK, yes, you want to run in at large scale in the data center.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Yes, we need to support different kind of hardware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: We had GPUs at that point. We had our first TPU at that point or was about to come out roughly around that time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So the design sort of included those. We had started to push on mobile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So we were running models on mobile. At that point, people were customizing code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So we wanted to make sure TensorFlow could support that as well so that that sort of became part of that overall design.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: When you say mobile, you mean like pretty complicated algorithms running on the phone?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: That's correct. So when you have a model that you deploy on the phone and run it there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So really at that time, there was ideas of running machine learning on the phone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: That's correct. We already had a couple of products that were doing that by then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: In those cases, we had basically customized handcrafted code or some internal libraries that we're using.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: Yeah. So in short, the way I like to think of this is our goals to enable machine learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And in a couple of ways, one is we have lots of exciting things going on in ML today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: So one is to, on the research side, keep pushing on the state of the art.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: The other is how do you take that across all the people outside who want to take that research and do some great things with it and integrate it to build real products, to have a real impact on people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And so that's the other axis in some ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: You know, at a high level, one way I think about it is there are a crazy number of computer devices across the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And we often used to think of ML and training and all of this as, okay, something you do either in the workstation or the data center or cloud.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: But we see things running on the phones, we see things running on really tiny chips, and we had some demos at the developer summit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And so the way I think about this ecosystem is how do we help get machine learning on every device that has a compute capability?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And that continues to grow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

metadata.title: Podcast: Rajat Monga: TensorFlow | Lex Fridman Podcast #22

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: The highly sensitive introvert tends to be philosophical

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: or spiritual in their orientation

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: rather than materialistic or hedonistic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: They dislike small talk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: They often describe themselves as creative or intuitive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: They dream vividly

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: and can often recall their dreams the next day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: They love music, nature, art and physical beauty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: They feel exceptionally strong emotions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: sometimes acute bouts of joy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: but also sorrow, melancholy and fear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: Highly sensitive people also process information

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: about their environments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: both physical and emotional, unusually deeply.

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: They tend to notice subtleties that others miss,

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: another person's shift in mood

metadata.title: Podcast: Susan Cain: The Power of Introverts and Loneliness | Lex Fridman Podcast #298

body.input: or a light bulb burning a touch too brightly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: What do you think we can learn from it

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: outside of the silliness of the actual application of it

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: to the autonomous vehicle?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: I think it's still an interesting ethical question

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and that in itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: just like much of the interaction with robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: has something to teach us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: But from your perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: do you think there's anything there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Well, I think you're right

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: that it does have something to teach us because,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: but I think what people are forgetting in all

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: of these conversations is the origins of the trolley problem

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and what it was meant to show us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: which is that there is no right answer

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and that sometimes our moral intuition

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: that comes to us instinctively

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: is not actually what we should follow

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: if we care about creating systematic rules

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: that apply to everyone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So I think that as a philosophical concept,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: it could teach us at least that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: but that's not how people are using it right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: We have, and these are friends of mine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and I love them dearly and their project adds a lot of value,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: but if we're viewing the moral machine project

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: as what we can learn from the trolley problems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: the moral machine is, I'm sure you're familiar,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: it's this website that you can go to

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and it gives you different scenarios like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: oh, you're in a car, you can decide to run over

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: these two people or this child.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: What do you choose?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Do you choose the homeless person?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Do you choose the person who's jaywalking?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: And so it pits these moral choices against each other

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and then tries to crowdsource

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: the quote unquote correct answer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: which is really interesting and I think valuable data,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: but I don't think that's what we should base

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: our rules in autonomous vehicles on

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: because it is exactly what the trolley problem

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: is trying to show,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: which is your first instinct might not be the correct one

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: if you look at rules that then have to apply

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: to everyone and everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So how do we encode these ethical choices

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: in interaction with robots?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So for example, autonomous vehicles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: there is a serious ethical question of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: do I protect myself?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Does my life have higher priority

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: than the life of another human being?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Because that changes certain controlled decisions

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: that you make.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So if your life matters more than other human beings,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: then you'd be more likely to swerve out of your current lane.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So currently automated emergency braking systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: that just break, they don't ever swerve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So swerving into oncoming traffic or no,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: just in a different lane can cause significant harm

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: to others, but it's possible that it causes less harm to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So that's a difficult ethical question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Do you have a hope that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: like the trolley problem is not supposed

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: to have a right answer, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Do you hope that when we have robots at the table,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: we'll be able to discover the right answer

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: for some of these questions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Well, what's happening right now, I think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: is this question that we're facing of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: what ethical rules should we be programming

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: into the machines is revealing to us

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: that our ethical rules are much less programmable

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: than we probably thought before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: And so that's a really valuable insight, I think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: that these issues are very complicated

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and that in a lot of these cases,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: you can't really make that call,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: like not even as a legislator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: And so what's gonna happen in reality, I think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: is that car manufacturers are just gonna try

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and avoid the problem and avoid liability

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: in any way possible, or they're gonna always protect

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: the driver because who's gonna buy a car

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: if it's programmed to kill you instead of someone else?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So that's what's gonna happen in reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: But what did you mean by, once we have robots at the table,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: do you mean when they can help us figure out what to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: No, I mean when robots are part of the ethical decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So no, no, not they help us, well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Oh, you mean when it's like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: should I run over a robot or a person?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Right, that kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So no, no, no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So it's exactly what you said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: which is when you have to encode the ethics

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: into an algorithm, you start to try to really understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: what are the fundamentals of the decision-making process

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: when you make certain decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Should you, like capital punishment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: should you take a person's life or not

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: to punish them for a certain crime?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: You can develop an algorithm to make that decision, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: And the hope is that the act of making that algorithm,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: however you make it, so there's a few approaches,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: will help us actually get to the core

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: of what is right and what is wrong under our current

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: societal standards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: But isn't that what's happening right now?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: And we're realizing that we don't have a consensus

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: on what's right and wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: You mean in politics in general?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Well, like when we're thinking about these trolley problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and autonomous vehicles and how to program ethics

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: into machines and how to make AI algorithms fair

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and equitable, we're realizing that this is so complicated

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and it's complicated in part because there doesn't seem

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: to be a one right answer in any of these cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Do you have a hope for, like one of the ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: of the moral machine is that crowdsourcing

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: can help us converge towards, like democracy

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: can help us converge towards the right answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Do you have a hope for crowdsourcing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Well, yes and no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So I think that in general, I have a legal background

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and policymaking is often about trying to suss out

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: what rules does this particular society agree on

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and then trying to codify that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So the law makes these choices all the time

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and then tries to adapt according to changing culture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: But in the case of the moral machine project,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: I don't think that people's choices on that website

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: necessarily reflect what laws they would want in place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: If given, I think you would have to ask them

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: a series of different questions in order to get up

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: what their consensus is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: I agree, but that has to do more

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: with the artificial nature of, I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: they're showing some cute icons on a screen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: That's almost, so if you, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: we would do a lot of work in virtual reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: And so if you put those same people into virtual reality

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: where they have to make that decision,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: their decision would be very different, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: I agree with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: That's one aspect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: And the other aspect is it's a different question

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: to ask someone, would you run over the homeless person

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: or the doctor in this scene,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: or do you want cars to always run over the homeless people?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: I think, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So let's talk about anthropomorphism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: To me, anthropomorphism, if I can pronounce it correctly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: is one of the most fascinating phenomena

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: from both the engineering perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and the psychology perspective, machine learning perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and robotics in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Can you step back and define anthropomorphism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: how you see it in general terms in your work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So anthropomorphism is this tendency that we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: to project human-like traits and behaviors

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and qualities onto non-humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: And we often see it with animals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: like we'll project emotions on animals

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: that may or may not actually be there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: We often see that we're trying to interpret things

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: according to our own behavior when we get it wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: But we do it with more than just animals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: We do it with objects, teddy bears,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: we see faces in the headlights of cars,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: and we do it with robots, very, very extremely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: You think that can be engineered?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Can that be used to enrich an interaction

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: between an AI system and a human?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: Oh yeah, for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: And do you see it being used that way often?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: I don't, I haven't seen, whether it's Alexa

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: or any of the smart speaker systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: often trying to optimize for the anthropomorphization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: You said you haven't seen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: I haven't seen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: They keep moving away from that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: I think they're afraid of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: They actually, so I only recently found out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: but did you know that Amazon has a whole team of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: who are just there to work on Alexa's personality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: So I know, it depends on your personality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: I didn't know that exact thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: but I do know that how the voice is perceived

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: is worked on a lot, if it's a pleasant feeling

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: about the voice, but that has to do more

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: with the texture of the sound and the audio and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: But personality is more like...

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: It's like, what's her favorite beer when you ask her?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: And the personality team is different

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: for every country too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: There's a different personality for German Alexa

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: than there is for American Alexa.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: That said, I think it's very difficult to use the,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: or really, really harness the anthropomorphism

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robotics | Lex Fridman Podcast #98

body.input: with these voice assistants

body.input: You and your son Christopher helped create the alien language in the movie Arrival.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Cellular Automata, Computation, and Physics | Lex Fridman Podcast #89

body.input: So let me ask maybe a bit of a crazy question, but if aliens were to visit us on Earth,
