body.input: And it is a really hard problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: To Titan, for example, like I said, it's one of the best studied atmospheres in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: solar system and people have tried to make these global circulation models and actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: predict what's going to happen moving into sort of the next season of Titan and those

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: predictions have ended up being wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And so then, you know, I don't know, it's always exciting when a prediction is wrong

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: because it means that there's something more to learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: Like your theory wasn't sufficient and then you get to go back and learn something by

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: how you have to modify the theory to make it fit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: I'm excited by the possibility one day there'll be for various moons and planets there'll

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: be like news programs reporting the weather with the fake confidence of like as if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: can predict the weather.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: We talked quite a bit about planets and moons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: Can we talk a little bit about asteroids?

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: For sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: What is, what's an asteroid and what kind of asteroids are there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So the asteroids, let's talk about just the restricted to the main asteroid belt, which

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: is the region.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: It's a region of debris basically between Mars and Jupiter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And the these sort of belts of debris throughout the solar system, the outer solar system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: you know, the Kuiper belt that we talked about, the asteroid belt, as well as certain other

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: populations where they accumulate because they're gravitationally more favored, are

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: remnant objects from the origin of the solar system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And so one of the reasons that we are so interested in them, aside from potentially the fact that

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: they could come hit Earth, but scientifically it's it gives us a window into understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: the composition of the material from which Earth and the other planets formed and how

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: that material was kind of redistributed over the history of the solar system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So the asteroids, one could classify them in two different ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: Some of them are ancient objects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So they accreted out of the sort of disk of material that the whole solar system formed

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: out of and have kind of remained ever since more or less the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: They've probably collided with each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And we see all these collisional fragments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And you can actually look and based on their orbits say, you know, like these 50 objects

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: originated as the same object.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: You can see them kind of dynamically moving apart after some big collision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And so some of them are these ancient objects maybe that have undergone collisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And then there's this other category of object that is the one that I personally find really

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: interesting, which is remnants of objects that could have been planets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So early on, a bunch of potential planets accreted that we call planetesimals, and they

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: formed and they formed with a lot of energy and they had enough time to actually differentiate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So some of these objects differentiated into cores and mantles and crests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And then they were subsequently disrupted in these massive collisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And now we have these fragments, we think fragments floating around the asteroid belt

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: that are like bits of mantle, bits of core, bits of crest basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So it's like puzzle pieces that you might be able to stitch together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: Or I guess it's all mixed up so you can't stitch together the original planet candidates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: Or is that possible to try to see if they kind of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: I mean, there's too many objects in there to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: I think that there are cases where people have kind of looked at objects and by looking

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: at their orbits, they say these objects should have originated together, but they have very

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: different compositions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And so then you can hypothesize maybe they were different fragments of a differentiated

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: object.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: But one of the really cool things about this is we've been talking about getting clues

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: into the interiors of planets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: We've never seen a planetary core or deep mantle directly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: Some mantle material comes up on our surface and then we can see it, but sort of in bulk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: We haven't seen these things directly and these asteroids potentially give us a chance

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: to look at what our own core and mantle is like, or at least would be like if it had

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: been also floating through space for a few billion years and getting irradiated and all

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: But it's a cool potential window or analogy into the interior of our own planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: How do you begin studying some of these asteroids?

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: If you were to put together a study, what are the interesting questions to ask that

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: are a little bit more specific?

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: Do you find a favorite asteroid that could be tracked and try to track it through telescopes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: Or do you have to land on those things to study it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So when it comes to the asteroids, there are so many of them and the big pictures or the

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: big questions are answered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So some questions can be answered by zooming in in detail on individual object, but mostly

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: you're trying to do a statistical study.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So you want to look at thousands of objects, even hundreds of thousands of objects, and

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: figure out what their composition is and look at how many big asteroids there are of this

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: composition versus how many small asteroids of this other composition and put together

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: these kind of statistical properties of the asteroid belt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And those properties can be directly compared with the results of simulations for the formation

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: of the solar system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: What do we know about the surfaces of asteroids or the contents of the insides of asteroids

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: and what are still open questions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So I would say that we don't know a whole lot about their compositions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: Most of them are small and so you can't study them in such detail with telescopes as you

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: could a planet or moon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And at the same time, because there are so many of them, you could send a spacecraft

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: to a few, but you can't really get a statistical survey with spacecraft.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And so a lot of what has been done comes down to classification.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: You look at how bright they are, you look at whether they're red or blue, simply whether

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: their spectrum is sloped towards long wavelengths or short wavelengths.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: There are certain, if you point a spectrograph at their surfaces, there are certain features

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: you can see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: So you can tell that some of them have silicates on them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: But these are the sort of, they're pretty basic questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: We're still trying to classify them based on fairly basic information in kind of combination

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: with our general understanding of the material the solar system formed from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: And so you're sort of, you're coming in with prior knowledge, which is that you more or

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: less know what the materials are the solar system formed from, and then you're trying

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: to classify them into these categories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: There's still a huge amount of room for understanding them better and for understanding how their

metadata.title: Podcast: Katherine de Kleer: Planets, Moons, Asteroids & Life in Our Solar System | Lex Fridman Podcast #184

body.input: surfaces are changing in the space environment.

body.input: Okay.

body.input: It doesn't appeal to me.

body.input: It doesn't answer the questions that I want answered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And it does so to such a strong case that when Roberto, Manguevera, Angra and I

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: began looking for principles, and I want to come back and talk about the use of principles in science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: because that's the other thing I was going to say and I don't want to lose that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: When we started looking for principles, we made our first principle,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: there is just one world and it happens once.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But so it's not helpful to my personal approach, to my personal agenda.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But of course, I'm part of a community.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And my sense of the many worlds interpretation, I have thought a lot about it and struggled a lot with it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: is the following. First of all, there's Everett himself, there's what's in Everett.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And there are several issues there connected with the derivation of the Born Rule,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: which is the rule that gives probabilities to events.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And the reasons why there is a problem with probability is that I mentioned the two ways

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: that physical systems can evolve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: The many worlds interpretation cuts off one, the one having to do with measurement,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and just has the other one, the Schrodinger evolution, which is the smooth evolution of the quantum state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But the notion of probability is only in the second rule, which we've thrown away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So where does probability come from?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I answer the question because experimentalists use probabilities to check the theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Now, at first sight, you get very confused because there seems to be a real problem

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: because in the many worlds interpretation, this talk about branches is not quite precise, but I'll use it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: There is a branch in which everything that might happen does happen with probability one in that branch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: You might think you could count the number of branches in which things do and don't happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and get numbers that you can define as something like frequentist probabilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And Everett did have an argument in that direction, but the argument gets very subtle

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: when there are an infinite number of possibilities, as is the case in most quantum systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And my understanding, although I'm not as much of an expert as some other people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: is that Everett's own proposal failed, did not work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: There are then, but it doesn't stop there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: There is an important idea that Everett didn't know about, which is decoherence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and it is a phenomenon that might be very much relevant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And so a number of people post Everett have tried to make versions of what you might call many worlds quantum mechanics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And this is a big area and it's subtle and it's not the kind of thing that I do well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So I consulted, that's why there's two chapters on this in the book I wrote.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Chapter 10, which is about Everett's version, and chapter 11.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: There's a very good group of philosophers of physics in Oxford,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Simon Sanders, David Wallace, Harvey Brown, and a number of others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And of course, there's David Deutsch, who is there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And those people have developed and put a lot of work into a very sophisticated set of ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: designed to come back and answer that question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: They have the flavor of, there are really no probabilities, we admit that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But imagine if the Everett story was true and you were living in that multiverse, how would you make bets?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And so they use decision theory from the theory of probability and gambling and so forth

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: to shape a story of how you would bet if you were inside an Everett universe and you knew that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And there is a debate among those experts as to whether they or somebody else has really succeeded.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And when I checked in as I was finishing the book with some of those people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: like Simon, who's a good friend of mine, and David Wallace,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: they told me that they weren't sure that any of them was yet correct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So that's what I put in my book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Now, to add to that, Sean has his own approach to that problem

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: in what's called self-referencing or self-locating observers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I tried to read it and it didn't make sense to me, but I didn't study it hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: I didn't communicate with Sean. I didn't do the things that I would do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So I had nothing to say about it in the book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: I don't know whether it's right or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Let's talk a little bit about science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: You mentioned the use of principles in science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: What does it mean to have a principle and why is that important?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: When I feel very frustrated about quantum gravity, I like to go back and read history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And of course, Einstein and his achievements are a huge lesson

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and hopefully something like a role model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And it's very clear that Einstein thought that the first job

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: when you want to enter a new domain of theoretical physics

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: is to discover and invent principles

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and then make models of how those principles might be applied in some experimental situation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: which is where the mathematics comes in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So for Einstein, there was no unified space and time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Minkowski invented this idea of space-time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: For Einstein, it was a model of his principles or his postulates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I've taken the view that we don't know the principles of quantum gravity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: I can think about candidates and I have some papers where I discussed

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: different candidates and I'm happy to discuss them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But my belief now is that those partially successful approaches

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: are all models which might describe indeed some quantum gravity physics

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: in some domain, in some aspect,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: but ultimately would be important because they model the principles

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and the first job is to tie down those principles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So that's the approach that I'm taking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So speaking of principles, in your 2006 book, The Trouble with Physics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: you criticized a bit string theory for taking us away from the rigors of the scientific method

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: or whatever you would call it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But what's the trouble with physics today and how do we fix it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Can I say how I read that book?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Because I'm not...

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: This, of course, has to be my fault because you can't, as an author,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: claim after all the work you put in that you were misread.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But I will say that many of the reviewers who are not personally involved

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and even many who were working on string theory or some other approach to quantum gravity

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: told me, communicated with me, and told me they thought that I was fair

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and balanced was the word that was usually used.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So let me tell you what my purpose was in writing that book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: which clearly got diverted by...

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: because there was already a rather hot argument going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: On which topic? On string theory specifically or in general in physics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: No, more specifically than string theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So since we're in Cambridge... Can I say that we're doing this in Cambridge?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Yeah, of course. Cambridge, just to be clear, Massachusetts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And on Harvard campus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Right. So Andy Strominger is a good friend of mine and has been for many, many years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And Andy... So originally there was this beautiful idea that there were five string theories

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and maybe they would be unified into one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And we would discover a way to break that symmetries of one of those string theories

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and discover the standard model and predict all the properties of the standard model particles

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: like their masses and charges and so forth, coupling constants.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And then there was a bunch of solutions to string theory found,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: which led each of them to a different version of particle physics with a different phenomenology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: These are called the Calabi-Yau manifolds, named after Yau, who was also here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Certainly we've been friends at some time in the past anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And then there were, nobody was sure, but hundreds of thousands of different versions of string theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And then Andy found there was a way to put a certain kind of mathematical curvature called torsion into the solutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And he wrote a paper, String Theory with Torsion, in which he discovered there was

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: not formally uncountable, but he was unable to invent any way to count the number of solutions or classify the diverse solutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And he wrote that this is worrying because doing phenomenology the old fashioned way by solving the theory

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: is not going to work because there's going to be loads of solutions for any proposed phenomenology for anything the experiments discovered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: It hasn't quite worked out that way. But nonetheless, he took that worry to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: We spoke at least once, maybe two or three times about that. And I got seriously worried about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And this is just a little...

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: It sounds like an anecdote that inspired your worry about string theory in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Well, I tried to solve the problem and I tried to solve the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: I was reading at that time a lot of biology, a lot of evolutionary theory, like Lindemar Gullis and Steve Gould and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I could take your time to go through the things, but it occurred to me maybe physics was like evolutionary biology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And maybe the laws evolved. And there was...

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: The biologists talk about a landscape, a fitness landscape of DNA sequences or protein sequences or species or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I took their concept and the word landscape from theoretical biology and made a scenario about how the universe as a whole

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: could evolve to discover the parameters of the standard model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I'm happy to discuss that. It's called cosmological natural selection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Cosmological natural selection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So the parameters of the standard model, so the laws of physics are changing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: This idea would say that the laws of physics are changing in some way that echoes that of natural selection or just it adjusts in some way towards some goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Yes. And I published that. I wrote the paper in the eight or 89. The paper was published in 92.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: My first book in 1997, The Life of the Cosmos, was explicitly about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I was very clear that what was important is that because you would develop an ensemble of universes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: but they were related by descent through natural selection, almost every universe would share the property that it was...

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Its fitness was maximized to some extent, or at least close to maximal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I could deduce predictions that could be tested from that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I worked all of that out and I compared it to the anthropic principle where you weren't able to make tests or make falsifications.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: All of this was in the late 80s and early 90s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: That's a really compelling notion. But how does that help you arrive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: I'm coming to where the book came from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Yes. So what got me... I worked on string theory. I also worked on loop quantum gravity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and I was one of the inventors of loop quantum gravity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And because of my strong belief in some other principles, which led to this notion of wanting a quantum theory of gravity

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: to be what we call relational or background independent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: I tried very hard to make string theory background independent and ended up developing a bunch of tools,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: which then could apply directly to general relativity, and that became loop quantum gravity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So the things were very closely related and have always been very closely related in my mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: The idea that there were two communities, one devoted to strings and one devoted to loops, is nuts and has always been nuts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Okay. So anyway, there's this nuts community of loops and strings that are all beautiful and compelling and mathematically speaking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And what's the trouble with all that? Why is that such a problem?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So I was interested in developing that notion of how science works based on a community and ethics that I told you about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I wrote a draft of a book about that, which had several chapters on methodology of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And it was a rather academically oriented book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And those chapters were the first part of the book, the first third of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And you can find their remnants in what's now the last part of the trouble with physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And then I described a number of test cases, case studies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And one of them, which I knew was the search for quantum gravity and string theory and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I was unable to get that book published.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So somebody made the suggestion of flipping it around and starting with the story of string theory, which was already controversial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: This was 2004, 2005.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But I was very careful to be detailed, to criticize papers and not people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: You won't find me criticizing individuals. You'll find me criticizing certain writing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But in any case, here's what I regret. Let me make your program worthwhile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: As far as I know, with the exception of not understanding how large the applications to condensed matter, say, of ADS-CFT would get,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: I think largely my diagnosis of string theory, as it was then, has stood up since 2006.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: What I regret is that the same critique, I was using string theory as an example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and the same critique applies to many other communities in science and know of, including, and this is what I regret, my own community.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: That is a community of people working on quantum gravity outside string theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I considered saying that explicitly, but to say that explicitly, since it's a small, intimate community,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: I would be telling stories and naming names and making a kind of history that I have no right to write.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: So I stayed away from that, but was misunderstood.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But if I may ask, is there a hopeful message for theoretical physics that we can take from that book, sort of that looks at the community,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: not just your own work, now with causality and nonlocality, but just broadly in understanding the fundamental nature of our reality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: What's your hope for the 21st century in physics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Well, do we solve the problem?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: That we solve the unfinished problem of Einstein's?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: That's certainly the thing that I care about most and hope for most.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Let me say one thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: Among the young people that I work with, I hear very often and sense a total disinterest in these arguments that we older scientists have

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: and an interest in what each other is doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And this is starting to appear in conferences where the young people interested in quantum gravity make a conference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: They invite loops and strings and causal dynamical triangulations and causal set people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And we're having a conference like this next week, a small workshop at perimeter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And I guess I'm advertising this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And then in the summer, we're having a big full-on conference, which is just quantum gravity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: It's not strings. It's not loops.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: But the organizers and the speakers will be from all the different communities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And this to me is very helpful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: That the different ideas are coming together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: At least people are expressing an interest in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: It's a huge honor talking to you, Lee. Thanks so much for your time today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lee Smolin: Quantum Gravity and Einstein's Unfinished Revolution | Lex Fridman Podcast #79

body.input: And now, here's my conversation with Zev Weinstein.

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: You've said that philosophy becomes more dangerous

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: in difficult times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: What do you mean by that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: Interestingly, I think I mean two things by that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: and I think firstly I should clarify.

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: When I say philosophy, I sort of mean

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: in a very traditional sense, just thinking, ideation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: and that could be reconsidering our notions of self

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: in a very traditional sense, which we consider philosophy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: or that could be technological innovation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: I think it's important to recognize all of these

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: as philosophies so that we can not question

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: whether it's important to promote thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: I think the other thing I should clarify

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: is when I say difficult times,

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: I mean times when nothing is growing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: and so the risk for real conflict is much greater

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: because people are incentivized to fight over the things

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: which already exist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: I think when times are not difficult,

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: the people with the greatest power

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: are usually the people who are very creative,

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: generating a lot, and that really requires ideation

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: or philosophy of some sort.

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: I think when times become stagnant,

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: the important successful people become the people

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: who are very good at protecting their own pieces of the pie

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: and taking others.

body.input: I think that those people have to be very opposed

metadata.title: Podcast: Zev Weinstein: The Next Generation of Big Ideas and Brave Minds | Lex Fridman Podcast #158

body.input: As part of MIT course 6S099 on artificial general intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: I got a chance to sit down with Christoph Koch, who is one of the seminal figures

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: in neurobiology, neuroscience, and generally in the study of consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: He is the president, the chief scientific officer of the Allen Institute for Brain Science in Seattle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: From 1986 to 2013, he was the professor at Caltech. Before that, he was at MIT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: He is extremely well cited, over 100,000 citations. His research, his writing, his ideas have had

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: big impact on the scientific community and the general public in the way we think about

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: consciousness, in the way we see ourselves as human beings. He's the author of several books,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: The Quest for Consciousness and Your Biological Approach, and a more recent book, Consciousness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2
