metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Okay, before we delve into the beautiful mysteries of consciousness, let's zoom out a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: And let me ask, do you think there's intelligent life out there in the universe?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Yes, I do believe so. We have no evidence of it, but I think the probabilities are overwhelming

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: in favor of it. Given the universe, well, we have 10 to the 11 galaxies and each galaxy has between

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: 10 to the 11, 10 to the 12 stars and we know more stars have one or more planets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: So how does that make you feel? It still makes me feel special because I have experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: I feel the world, I experience the world and independent of whether there are other creatures

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: out there, I still feel the world and I have access to this world in this very strange,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: compelling way and that's the core of human existence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Now you said human. Do you think if those intelligent creatures are out there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: do you think they experience their world? Yes, they are evolved if they are a product

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: of natural evolution as they would have to be. They will also experience their own world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: So consciousness isn't just human, you're right, it's much wider. It's probably,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: it may be spread across all of biology. We have, the only thing that we have special is we can talk

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: about it. Of course, not all people can talk about it. Babies and little children can talk about it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: patients who have a stroke in the left inferior frontal gyrus can talk about it, but most normal

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: adult people can talk about it and so we think that makes us special compared to little monkeys,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: the dogs, the cats, the mice, all the other creatures that we share the planet with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: But all the evidence seems to suggest that they too experience the world and so it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: like overwhelmingly likely that other aliens, that aliens would also experience their world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Of course, differently because they have a different sensorium, they have different sensors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: they have a very different environment. But the fact that I would strongly suppose that they also

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: have experiences, they feel pain and pleasure and see in some sort of spectrum and hear and have all

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: the other senses. Of course, their language, if they have one, would be different so we might not

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: be able to understand their poetry about the experiences that they have. That's correct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Right. So in a talk, in a video, I've heard you mention Suputsal, a Daxhound that you came up with,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: that you grew up with, it was part of your family when you were young. First of all,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: you're technically a Midwestern boy. You just-

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Technically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: But after that, you traveled around a bit, hence a little bit of the accent. You talked about Suputsal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: the Daxhound, having these elements of humanness, of consciousness that you discovered. So I just

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: wanted to ask, can you look back in your childhood and remember when was the first time you realized

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: you yourself, from a third person perspective, are a conscious being? This idea of stepping outside

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: yourself and seeing, there's something special going on here in my brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: I can't really, actually it's a good question. I'm not sure I recall a discrete moment. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: you take it for granted because that's the only world you know. The only world I know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: you know, is the world of seeing and hearing voices and touching and all the other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: So it's only much later, in my underguided days when I became, when I enrolled in physics and

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: in philosophy, that I really thought about it and thought, well, this is really fundamentally very,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: very mysterious. And there's nothing really in physics right now that explains this transition

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: from the physics of the brain to feelings. Where do the feelings come in? So you can look at the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: foundational equation of quantum mechanics, general relativity. You can look at the period table of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: the elements. You can look at the endless ATG seat chat in our genes and no way is consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Yet I wake up every morning to a world where I have experiences. And so that's the heart of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: the ancient mind-body problem. How do experiences get into the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: So what is consciousness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Experience. Consciousness is any experience. Some people call it subjective feeling. Some people

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: call it phenomenology. Some people call it qualia of the philosopher, but they all denote the same

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: thing. It feels like something in the famous word of the philosopher Thomas Nagel. It feels like

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: something to be a bat or to be, you know, an American or to be angry or to be sad or to be in

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: love or to have pain. And that is what experience is. Any possible experience. Could be as mundane

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: as just sitting in a chair. Could be as exalted as, you know, having a mystical moment, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: in deep meditation. Those are just different forms of experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Experience. So if you were to sit down with maybe the next skip a couple generations of IBM Watson,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: something that won Jeopardy. What is the gap, I guess the question is, between Watson,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: that might be much smarter than you, than us, than all any human alive, but may not have experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: What is the gap?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Well, so that's a big, big question. That's occupied people for the last, certainly last 50

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: years since we, you know, since the advent of birth of computers. That's a question Aaron Turing

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: tried to answer. And of course he did it in this indirect way by proposing a test, an operational

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: test. So, but that's not really, that's, you know, he tried to get it. What does it mean for a person

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: to think? And then he had this test, right? You lock them away and then you have a communication

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: with them. And then you try to, to guess after a while, whether that is a person or whether it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: a computer system. There's no question that now or very soon, you know, Alexa or Siri or, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Google now will pass this test, right? And you can game it, but, you know, ultimately, certainly in

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: your generation, there will be machines that will speak with complete poise. That will remember

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: everything you ever said. They'll remember every email you ever had, like, like Samantha, remember

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: in the movie, her, it's no question it's going to happen. But of course the key question is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: does it feel like anything to be Samantha in the movie, her or to, or does it feel like anything

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: to be Watson? And there one has to very, very strongly think there are two different concepts

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: here that we co-mingle. There is the concept of intelligence, natural or artificial, and there is

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: a concept of consciousness, of experience, natural or artificial. Those are very, very different

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: things. Now, historically, we associate consciousness with intelligence. Why? Because we live in a world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: leaving aside computers, of natural selection, where we are surrounded by creatures, either our

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: own kin that are less or more intelligent, or we go across species. Some are more adapted to

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: particular environment, others are less adapted, whether it's a whale or dog or you go talk about

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: a paramecium or a little worm, all right? And we see the complexity of the nervous system goes from

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: one cell to specialized cells to a worm that has three nets that have 30% of its cells are nerve

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: cells to a creature like us or like a blue whale that has 100 billion, even more nerve cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: And so, based on behavioral evidence and based on the underlying neuroscience, we believe that

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: as these creatures become more complex, they are better adapted to their particular ecological niche

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: and they become more conscious, partly because their brain grows. And we believe consciousness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: unlike the ancient, ancient people thought most, almost every culture thought that consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: with intelligence has to do with your heart. And you still to say that today, you see, honey,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: I love you with all my heart. But what you should actually say is, you say, no, honey,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: I love you with all my lateral hypothalamus. And for Valentine's Day, you should give your sweetheart

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: hypothalamic piece of chocolate, not a heart shaped chocolate, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Anyway, so we still have this language, but now we believe it's a brain. And so, we see brains of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: different complexity and we think, well, they have different levels of consciousness. They're capable

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: of different experiences. But now we confront a world where we know where we're beginning to

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: engineer intelligence and it's radical unclear whether the intelligence we're engineering has

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: anything to do with consciousness and whether it can experience anything. Because fundamentally,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: what's the difference? Intelligence is about function. Intelligence, no matter exactly how

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: you define it, sort of adaptation to new environments, being able to learn and quickly

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: understand the setup of this and what's going on and who are the actors and what's going to happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: next. That's all about function. Consciousness is not about function. Consciousness is about being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: It's in some sense, much fundamental. You can see folks that you can see this in several cases. You

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: can see it, for instance, in the case of the clinic. When you're dealing with patients who are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: let's say, had a stroke or were in a traffic accident, etc., they're pretty much immobile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Terri Schiavo, you may have heard historically, she was a person here in the 90s in Florida.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Her heart stood still. She was reanimated. Then for the next 14 years, she was what's called in

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: a vegetative state. So, there are thousands of people in a vegetative state. So, they're like

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: this. Occasionally, they open their eyes for two, three, four, five, six, eight hours and then close

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: their eyes. They have sleep-wake cycle. Occasionally, they have behavior. They do like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: but there's no way that you can establish a lawful relationship between what you say or the doctor

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: says or the mom says and what the patient does. So, there isn't any behavior. Yet, in some of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: these people, there is still experience. You can design and build brain machine interfaces where

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: you can see they still experience something. And of course, that these cases of locked in state,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: there's this famous book called The Diving Bell and the Butterfly where you had an editor,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: a French editor. He had a stroke in the brainstem, unable to move except his vertical eye movement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: He could just move his eyes up and down. He dictated an entire book. And some people even

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: lose this at the end. All the evidence seems to suggest that they're still in there. In this case,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: you have no behavior. You have consciousness. Second case is tonight, like all of us, you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: going to go to sleep. Close your eyes. You go to sleep. You will wake up inside your sleeping body

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: and you will have conscious experiences. They are different from everyday experience. You might fly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: You might not be surprised that you're flying. You might meet a long dead pet childhood dog,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: and you're not surprised that you're meeting them. But you have conscious experience of love,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: of hate. They can be very emotional. Your body during this state, typically to REM,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: state sends an active signal to your motor neurons to paralyze you. It's called atonia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Because if you don't have that, like some patients, what do you do? You act out your dreams.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: You get, for example, REM behavioral disorder, which is a bad juju to get.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Third case is pure experience. So I recently had this, what some people call a mystical experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: I went to Singapore and went into a flotation tank. So this is a big tub filled with water.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: That's body temperature and absent salt. You strip completely naked. You lie inside of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: You close the lid. Darkness. Complete darkness. Soundproof. So very quickly you become bodyless

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: because you're floating and you're naked. You have no rings, no watch, no nothing. You don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: feel your body anymore. There's no sound. Soundless. There's no photon. Sightless. Timeless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: Because after a while, early on, you actually hear your heart. But then you sort of adapt to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: And then sort of the passage of time ceases. And if you train yourself, like in a meditation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: not to think early on, you think a lot. It's a little bit spooky. You feel somewhat uncomfortable

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: or you think, well, I'm going to get bored. But if you try to not to think actively,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: you become mindless. So there you are. Bodyless. Timeless. Soundless. Sightless. Mindless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christof Koch: Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #2

body.input: But you're in a conscious experience. You're not asleep. You're not asleep. You are being a pure

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: otherwise known as GANs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And with his 2014 paper is responsible

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: for launching the incredible growth

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: of research and innovation

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: in this subfield of deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: He got his BS and MS at Stanford,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: his PhD at University of Montreal

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: with Yoshio Benjo and Aaron Kerville.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: He held several research positions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: including at OpenAI, Google Brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and now at Apple as the director of machine learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: This recording happened while Ian was still a Google Brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but we don't talk about anything specific to Google

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: or any other organization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: This conversation is part

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: of the Artificial Intelligence podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: or simply connect with me on Twitter

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: at Lex Friedman spelled F-R-I-D.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Ian Goodfellow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: You open your popular deep learning book

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: with a Russian doll type diagram

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that shows deep learning is a subset

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: of representation learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: which in turn is a subset of machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and finally a subset of AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So this kind of implies that there may be limits

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to deep learning in the context of AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So what do you think is the current limits of deep learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And are those limits something

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that we can overcome with time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Yeah, I think one of the biggest limitations

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: of deep learning is that right now it requires really

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: a lot of data, especially labeled data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: There are some unsupervised

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and semi-supervised learning algorithms

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that can reduce the amount of labeled data you need,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but they still require a lot of unlabeled data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Reinforcement learning algorithms, they don't need labels,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but they need really a lot of experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: As human beings, we don't learn to play Pong

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: by failing at Pong two million times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So just getting the generalization ability better

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: is one of the most important bottlenecks

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: in the capability of the technology today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And then I guess I'd also say deep learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: is like a component of a bigger system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So far, nobody is really proposing

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to have only what you'd call deep learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: as the entire ingredient of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: You use deep learning as sub-modules of other systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: like AlphaGo has a deep learning model

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that estimates the value function.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Most reinforcement learning algorithms

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: have a deep learning module

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that estimates which action to take next,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but you might have other components.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So you're basically building a function estimator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Do you think it's possible,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: you said nobody's kind of been thinking about this so far,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but do you think neural networks could be made to reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: in the way symbolic systems did in the 80s and 90s

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to do more, create more programs as opposed to functions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Yeah, I think we already see that a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I already kind of think of neural nets as a kind of program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I think of deep learning as basically learning programs

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that have more than one step.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So if you draw a flow chart

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: or if you draw a TensorFlow graph

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: describing your machine learning model,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I think of the depth of that graph

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: as describing the number of steps that run in sequence

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and then the width of that graph

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: is the number of steps that run in parallel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Now it's been long enough that we've had deep learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: working that it's a little bit silly

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to even discuss shallow learning anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: But back when I first got involved in AI,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: when we used machine learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: we were usually learning things like support vector machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: You could have a lot of input features to the model

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and you could multiply each feature by a different weight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: All those multiplications were done in parallel

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: There wasn't a lot done in series.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I think what we got with deep learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: was really the ability to have steps of a program

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that run in sequence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And I think that we've actually started to see

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that what's important with deep learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: is more the fact that we have a multi-step program

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: rather than the fact that we've learned a representation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: If you look at things like ResNuts, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: they take one particular kind of representation

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and they update it several times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Back when deep learning first really took off

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: in the academic world in 2006,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: when Jeff Hinton showed that you could train

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: deep belief networks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: everybody who was interested in the idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: thought of it as each layer

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: learns a different level of abstraction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: That the first layer trained on images

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: learns something like edges

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and the second layer learns corners.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And eventually you get these kind of grandmother cell units

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that recognize specific objects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Today, I think most people think of it more

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: as a computer program where as you add more layers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: you can do more updates before you output your final number.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: But I don't think anybody believes that layer 150

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: of the ResNet is a grandmother cell

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and layer 100 is contours or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Okay, so you're not thinking of it

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: as a singular representation that keeps building.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: You think of it as a program,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: sort of almost like a state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: The representation is a state of understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And yeah, I think of it as a program

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that makes several updates

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and arrives at better and better understandings,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but it's not replacing the representation at each step.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: It's refining it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And in some sense, that's a little bit like reasoning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: It's not reasoning in the form of deduction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but it's reasoning in the form of taking a thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and refining it and refining it carefully

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: until it's good enough to use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So do you think, and I hope you don't mind,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: we'll jump philosophical every once in a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Do you think of cognition, human cognition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: or even consciousness as simply a result

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: of this kind of sequential representation learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Do you think that can emerge?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Cognition, yes, I think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Consciousness, it's really hard

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to even define what we mean by that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I guess there's consciousness is often defined

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: as things like having self-awareness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and that's relatively easy to turn it

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: as something actionable for a computer scientist

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to reason about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: People also define consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: in terms of having qualitative states of experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: like qualia, and there's all these philosophical problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: like could you imagine a zombie

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: who does all the same information processing as a human,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but doesn't really have the qualitative experiences

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that we have?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: That sort of thing, I have no idea how to formalize

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: or turn it into a scientific question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I don't know how you could run an experiment

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to tell whether a person is a zombie or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And similarly, I don't know how you could run an experiment

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to tell whether an advanced AI system

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: had become conscious in the sense of qualia or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: But in the more practical sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: like almost like self-attention,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: you think consciousness and cognition

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: can in an impressive way emerge

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: from current types of architectures

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that we think of as learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Or if you think of consciousness in terms of self-awareness

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and just making plans based on the fact

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that the agent itself exists in the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: reinforcement learning algorithms

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: are already more or less forced

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to model the agent's effect on the environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So that more limited version of consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: is already something that we get limited versions of

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: with reinforcement learning algorithms

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: if they're trained well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: But you say limited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So the big question really is how you jump

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: from limited to human level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And whether it's possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Even just building common sense reasoning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: seems to be exceptionally difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So if we scale things up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: if we get much better on supervised learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: if we get better at labeling,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: if we get bigger data sets, more compute,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: do you think we'll start to see really impressive things

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that go from limited to something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: echoes of human level cognition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I think so, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I'm optimistic about what can happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: just with more computation and more data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I do think it'll be important to get the right kind of data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Today, most of the machine learning systems we train

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: are mostly trained on one type of data for each model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: But the human brain, we get all of our different senses

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and we have many different experiences

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: like riding a bike, driving a car,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: talking to people, reading.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I think when you get that kind of integrated data set,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: working with a machine learning model

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that can actually close the loop and interact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: we may find that algorithms not so different

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: from what we have today,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: learn really interesting things

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: when you scale them up a lot

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and train them on a large amount of multimodal data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So multimodal is really interesting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but within, like you're working adversarial examples,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: so selecting within one mode of data,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: selecting better at what are the difficult cases

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: from which you're most useful to learn from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Oh yeah, could we get a whole lot of mileage

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: out of designing a model that's resistant

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to adversarial examples or something like that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Right, that's the question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: My thinking on that has evolved a lot

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: over the last few years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: When I first started to really invest

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: in studying adversarial examples,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I was thinking of it mostly as adversarial examples

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: reveal a big problem with machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and we would like to close the gap

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: between how machine learning models respond

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to adversarial examples and how humans respond.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: After studying the problem more,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I still think that adversarial examples are important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I think of them now more of as a security liability

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: than as an issue that necessarily shows

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: there's something uniquely wrong with machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: as opposed to humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Also, do you see them as a tool

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to improve the performance of the system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Not on the security side, but literally just accuracy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I do see them as a kind of tool on that side,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but maybe not quite as much as I used to think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: We've started to find that there's a trade-off

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: between accuracy on adversarial examples

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and accuracy on clean examples.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Back in 2014, when I did the first adversarially trained

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: classifier that showed resistance

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to some kinds of adversarial examples,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: it also got better at the clean data on MNIST.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And that's something we've replicated

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: several times on MNIST,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that when we train against weak adversarial examples,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: MNIST classifiers get more accurate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: So far that hasn't really held up on other data sets

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and hasn't held up when we train against stronger adversaries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: It seems like when you confront

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: a really strong adversary,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: you tend to have to give something up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: But it's such a compelling idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: because it feels like that's how us humans learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to do the difficult cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: We try to think of what would we screw up

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and then we make sure we fix that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: It's also in a lot of branches of engineering,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: you do a worst case analysis

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and make sure that your system will work in the worst case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And then that guarantees that it'll work

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: in all of the messy average cases that happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: when you got into a really randomized world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Yeah, with driving with autonomous vehicles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: there seems to be a desire to just look for,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: think adversarially,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: try to figure out how to mess up the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And if you can be robust to all those difficult cases,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: then you can, it's a hand wavy empirical way

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to show your system is safe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Yeah, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Today most adversarial example research

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: isn't really focused on a particular use case,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but there are a lot of different use cases

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: where you'd like to make sure that the adversary

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: can't interfere with the operation of your system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Like in finance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: if you have an algorithm making trades for you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: people go to a lot of an effort to obfuscate their algorithm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: That's both to protect their IP

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: because you don't wanna research

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and develop a profitable trading algorithm

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: then have somebody else capture the gains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: But it's at least partly because you don't want people

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that make adversarial examples

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that fool your algorithm into making bad trades.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Or I guess one area that's been popular

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: in the academic literature is speech recognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: If you use speech recognition to hear an audio waveform

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: and then turn that into a command

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that a phone executes for you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: you don't want a malicious adversary

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: to be able to produce audio

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that gets interpreted as malicious commands,

body.input: especially if a human in the room doesn't realize

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that something like that is happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: In speech recognition, has there been much success

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: in being able to create adversarial examples

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that fool the system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Yeah, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: I guess the first work that I'm aware of

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: is a paper called Hidden Voice Commands

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that came out in 2016, I believe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: And they were able to show that they could make sounds

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that are not understandable by a human,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: but are recognized as the target phrase

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that the attacker wants the phone to recognize it as.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Since then, things have gotten a little bit better

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: on the attacker side and worse on the defender side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: It's become possible to make sounds

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: that sound like normal speech,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: than the human hears.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: The level of perceptibility

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: of the adversarial perturbation is still kind of high.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: When you listen to the recording,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

metadata.title: Podcast: Ian Goodfellow: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) | Lex Fridman Podcast #19

body.input: Yeah, so I tend to think of machine learning algorithms
