body.input: He was the CEO of Google for 10 years

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and a chairman for Six More,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: guiding the company through an incredible period of growth

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and a series of world-changing innovations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: He is one of the most impactful leaders

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: in the era of the internet and a powerful voice

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: for the promise of technology in our society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: It was truly an honor to speak with him

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: as part of the MIT course

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: on artificial general intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and the artificial intelligence podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Eric Schmidt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: What was the first moment

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: when you fell in love with technology?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I grew up in the 1960s as a boy

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: where every boy wanted to be an astronaut

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and part of the space program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So like everyone else of my age,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: we would go out to the cow pasture behind my house,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: which was literally a cow pasture,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and we would shoot model rockets off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And that I think is the beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And of course, generationally today,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: it would be video games and all the amazing things

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that you can do online with computers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: There's a transformative inspiring aspect of science and math

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that maybe rockets would bring

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: would instill in individuals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: You've mentioned yesterday,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: the eighth grade math is where the journey

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: through mathematical universe diverges for many people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: It's this fork in the roadway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: There's a professor of math at Berkeley, Edward Frankel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I'm not sure if you're familiar with him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I am.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: He has written this amazing book

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I recommend to everybody called Love and Math,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: two of my favorite words.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: He says that if painting was taught like math,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: then students would be asked to paint a fence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: which is his analogy of essentially how math is taught.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And so you never get a chance to discover the beauty

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of the art of painting or the beauty of the art of math.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So how, when and where did you discover that beauty?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I think what happens with people like myself

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: is that you're math enabled pretty early.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And all of a sudden you discover that you can use that

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: to discover new insights.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: The great scientists will all tell a story,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: the men and women who are fantastic today,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that somewhere when they were in high school or in college,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: they discovered that they could discover something themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And that sense of building something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of having an impact that you own,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: drives knowledge acquisition and learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: In my case, it was programming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And the notion that I could build things

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that had not existed, that I had built,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that it had my name on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And this was before open source,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: but you could think of it as open source contributions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So today, if I were a 16 or 17 year old boy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I'm sure that I would aspire as a computer scientist

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: to make a contribution like the open source heroes

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of the world today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: That would be what would be driving me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And I'd be trying and learning and making mistakes

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and so forth in the ways that it works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: The repository that represent, that GitHub represents

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and that open source libraries represent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: is an enormous bank of knowledge

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of all of the people who are doing that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And one of the lessons that I learned at Google

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: was that the world is a very big place

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and there's an awful lot of smart people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And an awful lot of them are underutilized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So here's an opportunity, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: building parts of programs, building new ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: to contribute to the greater of society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So in that moment in the 70s, the inspiring moment

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: where there was nothing and then you created something

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: through programming, that magical moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So in 1975, I think you've created a program called Lex,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: which I especially like because my name is Lex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So thank you, thank you for creating a brand

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that established a reputation that's long lasting, reliable

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and has a big impact on the world and still used today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So thank you for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: But more seriously, in that time, in the 70s,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: as an engineer, personal computers were being born.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Do you think you'd be able to predict the 80s, 90s

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and the odds of where computers would go?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I'm sure I could not and would not have gotten it right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I was the beneficiary of the great work of many, many people

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: who saw it clearer than I did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: With Lex, I worked with a fellow named Michael Lesk,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: who was my supervisor and he essentially helped me

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: architect and deliver a system that's still in use today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: After that, I worked at Xerox Palo Alto Research Center

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: where the Alto was invented and the Alto is the predecessor

body.input: of the modern personal computer or Macintosh and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And the Altos were very rare and I had to drive an hour

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: from Berkeley to go use them, but I made a point

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of skipping classes and doing whatever it took

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: to have access to this extraordinary achievement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I knew that they were consequential.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: What I did not understand was scaling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I did not understand what would happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: when you had 100 million as opposed to 100.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And so the, since then, and I have learned

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: the benefit of scale, I always look for things

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: which are going to scale to platforms, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So mobile phones, Android, all those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: There are, the world is a numerous,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: there are many, many people in the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: people really have needs, they really will use

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: these platforms and you can build big businesses

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: on top of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So it's interesting, so when you see a piece of technology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: now you think, what will this technology look like

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: when it's in the hands of a billion people?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: That's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So an example would be that the market is so competitive now

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that if you can't figure out a way for something

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: to have a million users or a billion users,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: it probably is not gonna be successful

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: because something else will become the general platform

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and your idea will become a lost idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: or a specialized service with relatively few users.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So it's a path to generality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: it's a path to general platform use,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: it's a path to broad applicability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Now there are plenty of good businesses that are tiny,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: so luxury goods, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: But if you wanna have an impact at scale,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: you have to look for things which are of common value,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: common pricing, common distribution

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and solve common problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: They're problems that everyone has.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And by the way, people have lots of problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Information, medicine, health, education, so forth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: work on those problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Like you said, you're a big fan of the middle class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Because there's so many of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: There's so many of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: By definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So any product, any thing that has a huge impact

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that improves their lives is a great business decision

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and it's just good for society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And there's nothing wrong with starting off in the high end

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: as long as you have a plan to get to the middle class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: There's nothing wrong with starting with a specialized

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: market in order to learn and to build and to fund things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So you start with a luxury market

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: to build a general purpose market.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: But if you define yourself as only a narrow market,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: someone else can come along with a general purpose market

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that can push you to the corner,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: can restrict the scale of operation, can force you to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: a lesser impact than you might be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So it's very important to think in terms of broad businesses

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and broad impact, even if you start

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: in a little corner somewhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So as you look to the 70s, but also in the decades to come,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and you saw computers, did you see them as tools?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Or was there a little element of another entity?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I remember a quote saying AI began with our dream

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: to create the gods.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Is there a feeling when you wrote that program

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that you were creating another entity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: giving life to something?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I wish I could say otherwise,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: but I simply found the technology platforms so exciting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: That's what I was focused on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I think the majority of the people that I've worked with,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and there are a few exceptions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Steve Jobs being an example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: really saw this as a great technological play.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I think relatively few of the technical people

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: understood the scale of its impact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So I used NCP, which is a predecessor to TCPIP.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: It just made sense to connect things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: We didn't think of it in terms of the internet

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and then companies and then Facebook and then Twitter

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and then politics and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: We never did that build.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: We didn't have that vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And I think most people, it's a rare person

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: who can see compounding at scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Most people can see,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: if you ask people to predict the future,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: they'll say, they'll give you an answer

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of six to nine months or 12 months,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: because that's about as far as people can imagine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: But there's an old saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: which actually was attributed to a professor at MIT

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: a long time ago,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that we overestimate what can be done in one year,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and we underestimate what can be done in a decade.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And there's a great deal of evidence

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that these core platforms at hardware and software

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: take a decade, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So think about self-driving cars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Self-driving cars were thought about in the 90s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: There were projects around them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: The first DARPA Challenge was roughly 2004.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So that's roughly 15 years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And today we have self-driving cars

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: operating in a city in Arizona, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So 15 years, and we still have a ways to go

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: before they're more generally available.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So you've spoken about the importance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: You just talked about predicting into the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: You've spoken about the importance

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of thinking five years ahead

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and having a plan for those five years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: The way to say it is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: almost everybody has a one-year plan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Almost no one has a proper five-year plan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And the key thing to having a five-year plan

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: is having a model for what's going to happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: under the underlying platforms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So here's an example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Moore's law as we know it, the thing that powered

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: improvements in CPUs, has largely halted

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: in its traditional shrinking mechanism

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: because the costs have just gotten so high.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: It's getting harder and harder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: But there's plenty of algorithmic improvements

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and specialized hardware improvements.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So you need to understand the nature of those improvements

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and where they'll go in order to understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: how it will change the platform.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: In the area of network connectivity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: what are the gains that are going to be possible in wireless?

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: It looks like there's an enormous expansion

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of wireless connectivity at many different bands.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And that we will primarily,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: historically I've always thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that we were primarily going to be using fiber,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: but now it looks like we're going to be using fiber

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: plus very powerful high bandwidth

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: sort of short distance connectivity

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: to bridge the last mile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: That's an amazing achievement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: If you know that, then you're going to build your systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: differently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: By the way, those networks have different latency properties

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: because they're more symmetric.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: The algorithms feel faster for that reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And so when you think about whether it's fiber

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: or just technologies in general,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: so there's this barber, wooden poem or quote

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that I really like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: It's from the champions of the impossible

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: rather than the slaves of the powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: The impossible rather than the slaves of the possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that evolution draws its creative force.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So in predicting the next five years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: I'd like to talk about the impossible and the possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Well, and again, one of the great things about humanity

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: is that we produce dreamers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Right, we literally have people who have a vision

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and a dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: They are, if you will, disagreeable

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: in the sense that they disagree with the,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: they disagree with what the sort of zeitgeist is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: They say there is another way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: They have a belief, they have a vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: If you look at science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: science is always marked by such people

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: who went against some conventional wisdom,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: collected the knowledge at the time

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and assembled it in a way that produced a powerful platform.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And you've been amazingly honest about,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: in an inspiring way about things you've been wrong

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: about predicting and you've obviously been right

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: about a lot of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: But in this kind of tension,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: how do you balance as a company

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: in predicting the next five years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: the impossible, planning for the impossible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So listening to those crazy dreamers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: letting them do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: letting them run away and make the impossible real,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: make it happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And slow, you know, that's how programmers often think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And slowing things down and saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: well, this is the rational,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: this is the possible, the pragmatic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: the dreamer versus the pragmatist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So it's helpful to have a model

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: which encourages a predictable revenue stream,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: as well as the ability to do new things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So in Google's case, we're big enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and well enough managed and so forth

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that we have a pretty good sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of what our revenue will be for the next year or two,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: at least for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And so we have enough cash generation

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that we can make bets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And indeed, Google has become alphabet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So the corporation is organized around these bets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And these bets are in areas of fundamental importance

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: to the world, whether it's artificial intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: medical technology, self-driving cars,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: connectivity through balloons, on and on and on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And there's more coming and more coming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So one way you can express this is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: the current business is successful enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that we have the luxury of making bets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And another one that you could say is that we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: the wisdom of being able to see that a corporate structure

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: needs to be created to enhance the likelihood

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of the success of those bets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So we essentially turned ourselves into a conglomerate

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: of bets and then this underlying corporation, Google,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: which is itself innovative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So in order to pull this off,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: you have to have a bunch of belief systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And one of them is that you have to have bottoms up

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and tops down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: The bottoms up we call 20% time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And the idea is that people can spend 20% of the time

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And the top down is that our founders in particular

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: have a keen eye on technology

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: and they're reviewing things constantly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So an example would be they'll hear about an idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: or I'll hear about something and it sounds interesting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: let's go visit them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: to see if that's possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And if you do this long enough,

body.input: you get pretty good at predicting what's likely to work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So that's a beautiful balance that struck.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: Is this something that applies at all scale?

body.input: So in the fair-

body.input: Seems to be.

body.input: That Sergey, again, 15 years ago,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: that you needed that 10% to make the sum of the growth work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And it turns out he was right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: So getting into the world of artificial intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: And when I was a PhD student, I studied AI a bit

body.input: and it entered, during my looking at it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: is that there's no single formula for leadership.

body.input: That's more who I am, somewhat more conservative,

body.input: more thorough in execution, a little bit more risk averse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Eric Schmidt: Google | Lex Fridman Podcast #8

body.input: There's also people who are sort of slightly insane, right?

body.input: and they feel it and they drive it and so forth.

body.input: And now, dear friends, here's biology, Srinivasan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: At the core of your belief system is something you call the prime number maze.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: I'm curious, I'm curious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: We've got to start there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: If we can start anywhere, it's with mathematics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Let's go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: All right, great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: A rat can be trained to turn at every even number or every third number in a maze to

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: get some cheese.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: But evidently, it can't be trained to turn at prime numbers, two, three, five, seven,

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: and then 11, and so on and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: That's just too abstract.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And frankly, if most humans were dropped into a prime number maze, they probably wouldn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: be able to figure it out either.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: They'd have to start counting and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Actually, pretty difficult to figure out what the turning rule was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Yet, the rule is actually very simple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And so, the thing I think about a lot is just how many patterns in life are we just like

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: these rats and we're trapped in a prime number maze?

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And if we had just a little bit more cogitation, if we had a little bit more cognitive ability,

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: a little bit more, whether it's brain machine interface or just better physics, we could

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: just figure out the next step in that prime number maze.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: We could just see it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: We could just see the grid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And that's what I think about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: That's a big thing that drives me, is figuring out how we can actually conceive, understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: that prime number maze that we're living in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: So, understand which patterns are just complex enough that they are beyond the limit of human

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And what do you make of that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Are the limits of human cognition a feature or a bug?

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: I think mostly a bug.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: I admire Ramanujan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: I admire Feynman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: I admire these great mathematicians and physicists who were just able to see things that others

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: couldn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And just by writing it down, that's a leap forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: People talk about it's not the idea of its execution, but that's for trivial ideas, for

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: great ideas, for Maxwell's equations or Noon's laws or quantum electrodynamics or some of

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Ramanujan's identities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: That really does bring us forward, especially when you can check them and you don't know

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: how they work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: You have the phenomenological, but you don't have the theory underneath it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And then that stimulates the advancement of theory to figure out why is this thing actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: working.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And then the epistemic arose in part from the phenomenological studies that were basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: being done where people are just getting steam engines and so on to work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And then they abstracted out thermodynamics and so on from that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: So the practice led the theory rather than vice versa to some extent that's happening

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: in neural networks now, as you're aware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And I think that's...

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: So just something that's true and that works, even if we don't know yet, that's amazing

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: and it pulls us forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: So I do think that the limits are more of a bug than a feature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Is there something that humans will never be able to figure out about our universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: about the theory, about the practice of our universe?

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: People will typically quote Gridell's incompleteness for such a question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And yeah, there are things that are provably unknowable or provably unprovable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: But I think you can often get an approximate solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: The Hillebert...

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Hillebert's problem is like, we will know, we must know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: At least we should know that we can't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Push to get at least an approximate solution, push to know that we can't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: At least we push back that darkness enough so that we have lit up that corner of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: intellectual universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Let's actually take a bit of a tangent and explore a bit in a way that I did not expect

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: we would.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: But let's talk about the nature of reality briefly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: I don't know if you're familiar with the work of Don Hoffman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: No, I don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: I know Roger Penrose has his Road to Reality series for basic physics getting up to everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: we know, but go ahead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Tell me about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: It's even wilder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: When we started doing physics, we started to question of what is fundamental and what

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: is emergent in this beautiful universe of ours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And there's a bunch of folks who think that space-time, as we know it, the four-dimensional

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: space is emergent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: It's not fundamental to the physics of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: And the same, many argue, I think Sean Carroll is one of them, is that time itself, the way

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: we experience it is also emergent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: It's not fundamental to the way our universe works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Anyway, those are the technical term, I apologize for swearing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Those are the mind fucks of modern physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: But if we stroll along that road further, we get somebody like Donald Hoffman, who makes

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: the evolutionary case that the reality we perceive with our eyes is not only an abstraction

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: of objective reality, but it's actually completely detached.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: We're in a video game, essentially, that's consistent for all humans, but it's not at

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: all connected to physical reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: It's an illusion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: It's like a version of the simulation hypothesis?

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: In a very distant way, but the simulation says that there's a sort of computational

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: nature to reality, and then there's a programmer that creates this reality and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: He says that we humans have a brain that is able to perceive the environment, and evolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: is produced from primitive life to complex life on earth, produce the kind of brain that

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: doesn't at all need to sense the reality directly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: So this table, according to Donald Hoffman, is not there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Not just as an abstraction, we don't sense the molecules that make up the table, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: all of this is fake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: So I tend to be more of a hard science person, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Just on that, people talk about qualia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Is your perception of green different from my perception of green?

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: My counter argument on that is, well, we know something about spectrum of light, and we

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: can build artificial eyes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: If we can build artificial eyes, which we can, they're not amazing, but you can actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: We can build artificial ears and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Obviously, we can build recording devices and for cameras and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Well, operationally, the whole concept of your perception of green, you see green as

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: purple, I see green as green, or what I call green, doesn't seem to add up because it

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: does seem like we can do engineering around it, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: So the Hoffman thing, I get why people more broadly will talk about a simulation hypothesis

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: because it's like Feynman and many others have talked about how math is surprisingly

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: useful to describe the world, like very simple equations give rise to these complex phenomena.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Wolfram is also on this from a different angle with the cellular automata stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: But-

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: It's almost suspicious how well it works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Yeah, but on their hand, it's like, yet we're still also in a prime number maze.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: There's things we just don't understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: So within the constraints of the non-prime numbers, we find math to be extremely effective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: surprisingly effective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: Yeah, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: on.

body.input: after just a few years of not necessarily even continuous service.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

body.input: thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331

metadata.title: Podcast: Balaji Srinivasan: How to Fix Government, Twitter, Science, and the FDA | Lex Fridman Podcast #331
